50 Under $50: Your Ultimate Southern Holiday Gift Guide

We're back with our annual "50 Under $50" holiday gift guide, featuring makers and retailers we love across the South!

November 23, 2026 · By Zoe Yarborough
6
0
Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest
Add StyleBlueprint on Google
Pin
Share with your friends!

SHARES

Instaread

Some of the best gifts are the ones that make you say, “Wait, where did you find that?” Keeping with StyleBlueprint’s yearly tradition, we shopped Southern makers and stores for 50 FINDS — all priced at $50 or less. There’s plenty here for the host, the hard-to-shop-for, and the kid who already has everything. And if a little something for yourself sneaks into the cart, we get it.

Table of Contents
  1. SIPS & SNACKS
  2. KITCHEN & ENTERTAINING
  3. HOME DECOR
  4. WOMEN’S WARDROBE & JEWELRY BOX
  5. BATH & BEAUTY
  6. MEN
  7. KIDS
  8. PETS

We are grateful to all our sponsors:

SIPS & SNACKS

Southern Chili Crisp

For friends who like a little kick with everything, this Southern Chili Crisp ($20 a jar) by Red Clay brings the heat and crunch. Made with peanuts, garlic, shallots, and Fresno chili flakes, it’s delicious spooned over everything from fried eggs and avocado toast to noodles and fried chicken.

Mini dark chocolate bars

Tuck one of these into every stocking and keep a couple for yourself. Spring & Mulberry’s Pure Dark Minis are made with 72% cacao, sweetened with dates, and come in a dozen for $40.56.

Heirloom finishing salt

J.Q. Dickinson’s heirloom Appalachia-made, flaky finishing salt looks pretty and tastes even better. A 1-ounce jar ($6.50), a 3.5-ounce jar ($12), or a 1-pound bag ($28) would make a chic gift paired with a thrifted vintage vessel.

Callie’s cinnamon biscuits

Every holiday host appreciates an unfussy breakfast for the morning after. Handmade in Charleston and layered with butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon, Callie’s cinnamon biscuits arrive fully baked and ready to reheat. They’re also a delicious doorstep surprise for neighbors. A 24-pack is $49.95.

We are grateful to all our sponsors:

Bear Mix

Put out a bowl of Bear Food’s Gourmet Bear Mix ($19.95 for 10 ounces) and watch everyone start picking out their favorite bits. We’re going straight for the spicy cheddar Cajun sticks and toffee peanuts.

Classic Tonic Syrup

One of the world’s most ubiquitous gin companions is made in Kentucky. Pour a proper G&T with a set of Jack Rudy Cocktail Co.’s ($32) Classic Tonic Syrup, featuring real cane sugar and a delicate blend of botanicals.

Asheville Mix Popcorn

Poppy’s Asheville Mix settles the sweet-or-salty debate by popping white cheddar and salted caramel popcorn in the same bag. Asheville illustrator Annie Riker designed the wrapper, and $1 from each $9.95 bag sold helps small businesses in western North Carolina continue rebuilding after Hurricane Helene.

Cheerwine Holiday Punch

Show up with a case of this, and you’ve got the kids’ table and the grown-ups covered. A 24-pack of Cheerwine‘s fizzy seasonal punch is $20. IYKYK, y’all.

KITCHEN & ENTERTAINING

Happy people mug

Gift this happy mug to your arty friends, paired with a pound of local coffee beans. Each mug is hand-painted in Metairie, LA, and costs $50 at Home Malone.

Cocktail napkins

This delightful set of embroidered linen cocktail napkins is $44 at Peddler Interiors, and we’d bring them to the party tied around a bottle of bubbly.

Set of cocktail glasses

A round of martinis feels a little more old Hollywood in Pappy & Company’s Nick and Nora glasses ($30 for the pair). Your spirit-forward recipient will likely spot the signature three keys etched into the base.

We are grateful to all our sponsors:

Jersey tea towel

Slow-fashion textile designer Alabama Chanin wastes nothing, and these soft organic-cotton jersey tea towels, crafted in Florence, AL, make the perfect gift for the hard-to-shop-for foodie. They come in a bunch of colors for $38.

Ruffle spoon rest

Give that sauce-covered wooden spoon somewhere cute to sit, like this $14 stoneware spoon rest from Magnolia. It has a speckled gray glaze and a ruffled rim, pretty enough to leave out after the dinner party mess is cleaned up.

HOME DECOR

Dough bowl candle

You can’t go wrong with a dough bowl candle in a wintry scent. Georgia-based Southern E-Scentuals has dreamy seasonal options for $44.99 each, like Holiday Cheer, Roasted Pinecones, Garland & Tinsel, and Hearth & Home. Your giftee can use their rustic wooden vessels on a coffee table or mantel after the candle burns.

Olive jar ornament

For the friend who takes their martini extra dirty, this hand-blown glass olive jar deserves a spot on the tree. Hand-painted details and lifelike olives make it a charming little conversation piece, and the retro holiday box is cute enough to skip the wrapping paper. It’s $22 at Christopher Todd.

Moisture meter

For the plant parent in your life, this cheerfully hued moisture meter takes the guesswork out of greenery tending. Simply insert the probe into the soil and check the dial. No batteries required! It’s a practical little gift from Millstone Nursery for $18.

Ceramic vase

A few flowering branches are all it takes to make this Emerson Creek Pottery vase ($32.50) a centerpiece. Handmade in Virginia, the deep-blue stoneware works year-round.

Glass suncatchers

Blenko Glass Company’s handblown glassware is typically more of a splurge than under-$50, but these cute suncatchers (that can also double as ornaments!) in clover-green glass are currently on sale for $18.70 (reg. $22).

Holiday ornament frame

A printed photo? In a frame? Ready to hang on the tree? You’re winning Christmas with this $35 red-and-green daisy ornament from Charlotte’s. The magnetic design lets you add a photo to each side and easily swap them out over the years.

Cowboy Christmas candle

Imagine: with the tree in the stand, and a cocktail in hand, you press play on your favorite holiday record for the first time all season. This is that scent. Ranger Station’s $39 Cowboy Christmas candle sells out for a reason. Montana juniper, amber, frankincense, and a splash of whiskey, all poured by hand in Nashville.

We are grateful to all our sponsors:

Embroidery kit

Cue up an audiobook, put the kettle on, and settle into a little stitching. Each Cozyblue embroidery kit includes a preprinted pattern, floss, needle, hoop, and instructions for turning a quiet evening into something cute enough to hang. There are dozens of patterns for $28 each, but we love this book-themed one.

WOMEN’S WARDROBE & JEWELRY BOX

Jewelry organizer

Untangling necklaces is a lousy way to start a vacation. Atlanta accessory darling INK+ALLOY’s $36 Maddie Jewelry Roll tucks chains, hoops, and rings into separate pockets and comes in a bunch of great color combos.

Wrap ring

This hammered brass (or silver) wrap ring is $20 at Joffa, a Memphis-based non-profit artisan marketplace with an incredible mission. The ring adjusts to fit, so you can skip the covert ring-size detective work. Refugee and immigrant women make each ring by hand and earn fair wages for their work.

Mini bolo charm

This handmade bolo charm — $17.99 from PokeyBoloCo on Etsy — loops around a boot’s pull strap or purse handle for an instant pop of Western flair.

We are grateful to all our sponsors:

Fish lapel pin

For the angler who cleans up nicely, these miniature fish pins bring a little personality to a sweater or jacket lapel. Choose a favorite catch, from largemouth bass to catfish or redfish, each handmade in South Louisiana. The bronze pins are $48 each at MIMOSA Handcrafted.

Stackable gold bangle

A classic gold bangle is always a welcome addition to a jewelry box. The Henley ($40 each before first-order discounts) from Dallas-based Allie + Bess looks lovely worn solo, alongside a watch, or stacked with others. Finished in 14-karat gold plating, it also comes in three sizes for a more personalized fit.

Green stone bracelet

A little green, a little gold, and plenty of everyday appeal. These lightweight clay heishi bracelets pair earthy green beads with a gleaming gold-toned accent. Wear one solo or stack a few for a bolder look. Find them for $45 each (and in many colors and shapes to mix and match) at Gabrielle’s.

Bandana

Designed in North Carolina and handcrafted in India, this lightweight bandana features hand-drawn desert flowers and the “kickin’ up dust” mantra, adding personality to a simple outfit. Tie it around your neck or in your hair for an easy style upgrade by Jenni Earle. It’s currently on sale for $33.60 (reg. $42).

Striped slouchy top

Bold latte-and-butter stripes give this relaxed long-sleeve top an effortlessly cool look. Pair it with a colored skirt or jeans for an easy weekend outfit, or gift it to the friend whose closet always has room for another stripe. It’s $42.99 at Ramble & Co.

Rope belt

For the roomy shirtdress we love but always feel needs something, ExVoto Vintage’s $39 rope belt comes in four colors and can easily tighten a looser look or slide through belt loops for a tasseled accessory.

Scalloped pants

Could these black gingham, scalloped-hem cuties really be on this list? Yep! The $49.99 Becky pants from Tin Roof Gift Shop have wide legs, an elastic waist, and side pockets, and offer the perfect put-together-but-still-comfy look we crave.

We are grateful to all our sponsors:

BATH & BEAUTY

Verb hair oil

Having fully switched to this Austin-based hair care line on my stylist’s recommendation, I can safely say it’s changed my life. The Verb hair oil ($22) is an everyday elixir that adds some sleek shine and bounce, whether you’re air-drying or styling.

Sweet Grace bath soak

These mineral soaking salts bring SC-based Bridgewater Candle Co.’s most popular fragrance to bath time, blending fruity passionfruit and apricot with cozy notes of tea, vanilla, and patchouli. A two-pound $25 bag makes a lovely gift for anyone craving a little at-home indulgence.

Detangler hairbrush

Before your bag eats another hair tie, you’ll be glad you stashed a spare in your brush. The $16.99 TELETIES detangler brush has a hidden compartment and a built-in mirror for a quick ponytail redo on the go.

Mini perfume roller

I stock up on mini-size perfume rollers for my bags, car, and drawers throughout the house. This Maison Louise Marie mini in Bois de Balincourt is the perfect stocking stuffer and a known dupe for Le Labo Santal 33, so you’ll get even more brownie points. It’s $20 at Baker Tatum.

Cosmetic bag

A tiger tangled in Christmas lights is perfect for the maximalist or product lover on your list. This $38 cosmetic bag from Judith March would be so cute with a cherry-red lip gloss tucked inside before you wrap it.

We are grateful to all our sponsors:

Crumb catchers

We love practical, unexpected gifts. Toss these little orbs down into your purse, and they catch all the lint and crumbs! Then you can wash and reuse them. Genius for moms and friends who throw everything into their bags every time they leave the house. A pair of two is $14.95 at Southern Roots.

MEN

Hand-forged catchall

Even life’s random detritus deserves a handsome place to land. Starting at $50 on Etsy, MadeByKourmoulis’s hand-forged catchall gives keys, coins, and rings a proper home, with a hammered finish and optional personalized marks for extra meaning.

Three-in-one fish bottle opener

A little bar-cart, cooler, or tailgate addition for your favorite guy. It looks like a little wooden fish, but it has a corkscrew, beer cap opener, and small blade for cutting foil. It comes in a gift box and would be especially thoughtful as a host gift paired with a bottle of wine. It’s $28 at Smyth’s Jeweler.

Leather tag

Atlanta-based KMM & CO crafts all kinds of leather goods, and this classic, versatile tag ($20), made from belting-weight leather, can be embossed with a name, initials, or short phrase. He can use it as a bookmark, luggage identifier, or key chain.

Cocktail smoker

Give their usual Old Fashioned a little barroom drama with the Foghat Cocktail Smoker. It sits right on the glass, so they can add just a whisper of oak smoke or go full campfire. Find it at Bird’s Nest Florist & Gifts for $40.

Olive rope hat

For the guy who’s rarely without a hat, this olive option brings a classic touch to his everyday rotation. A structured front and rope detail give it a retro feel, while an adjustable strap with a metal buckle keeps the fit comfortable. It’s $40 from Oxford-based GenTeal.

Socks

You can find every motif under the sun on a sock these days, but this tortoise-and-hare design feels especially clever in comfy pima cotton. The pair is $24 from Bird Dog Bay.

KIDS

Western sand jar

A little Wild West adventure, all packed into a jar! This sensory set pairs moldable sand with miniature horses, cacti, and other themed treasures for imaginative play. It’s a fun, hands-on gift for the little cowboy or cowgirl on your list. Find this at Selah James for $21.

Ukulele

For the little musician ready for a living-room debut, Emerson & Friends offers a wooden toy ukulele with four soft nylon strings, available in terracotta (pictured) or slate blue for $34.99.

Slippers

Christmas-morning PJs deserve equally cute slippers. Weezie’s plush kids’ pair starts at $48 and comes in green plaid (pictured), coral hearts, blue stripes, and even leopard, with elastic heel straps to keep them on through the dash to the tree.

Kindness chain

Encourage little good deeds that add up to something worth hanging on the mantel with The Kindness Chain. Each colorful link suggests an act of kindness for kids to complete, creating a growing garland of good intentions put into practice for $15 at Home + Vine.

DIY Ferris wheel

The whole family will huddle around the kitchen table, building this intricate Ferris wheel ($49.99 from Tabla Rasa Toys). With more than 950 pieces to tinker with, you get a nearly 14-inch wheel that spins and plays a tune.

PETS

Funky dog collar

This $25 waterproof collar from Austin-based Springland Pets lets four-legged pals accessorize, too. With the $3 silicone charms, bold stripes, and color combos, what’s not to love?

Silhouette ornament

Patti at Heart Paper Scissors will put your pet or child’s silhouette on a beautiful ornament with custom text to commemorate each year. What a great gifting tradition to start for $32.

Happy gifting!
